H7634.name: Sachia
H7634.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7634.short: Sachia was a son of Shaharaim, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

H7687H.name: Segub
H7687H.brief: Son of Hezron; father of Jair
H7687H.short: Segub, son of Hezron, was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in Gilead.

H7687G.name: Segub
H7687G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7687G.short: Segub was the son of Hiel, who rebuilt Jericho during Ahab's reign.

H7678G.name: Shabbethai
H7678G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7678G.brief: Levite who opposed Ezra's marriage reforms
H7678G.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, opposed Ezra's efforts to address the issue of intermarriage among the returned exiles.

H7678I.name: Shabbethai
H7678I.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7678I.brief: Levite in charge of external affairs in Jerusalem
H7678I.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, was responsible for overseeing external affairs in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

H7678H.name: Shabbethai
H7678H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7678H.brief: Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
H7678H.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, assisted in explaining the Law to the people during the public reading led by Ezra.

H7610.name: Shear-jashub
H7610.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7610.short: Shear-jashub, meaning "a remnant shall return," was the son of the prophet Isaiah and accompanied his father to meet King Ahaz.

H7652G.name: Sheba
H7652G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7652G.brief: Gadite leader during the reign of Jotham
H7652G.short: Sheba was one of the Gadite leaders who lived in Bashan during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah.

H7652A.name: Sheba
H7652A.desc: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
H7652A.short: Sheba, a Benjamite, led a rebellion against King David but was ultimately defeated, and his head was delivered to Joab.

H7614H.name: Sheba
H7614H.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H7614H.brief: Descendant of Joktan, settling in southern Arabia
H7614H.short: Sheba, a descendant of Joktan, is associated with the ancient kingdom of Sheba in southern Arabia, known for its wealth and trade.

H7614G.name: Sheba
H7614G.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H7614G.brief: Descendants of Cush, known for wealth and trade
H7614G.short: The Sabeans, descendants of Cush, were known for their wealth, trade in spices and precious stones, and were mentioned in various contexts throughout the Old Testament.

H7614I.name: Sheba
H7614I.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H7614I.short: Sheba was one of the sons of Jokshan, a descendant of Abraham through his wife Keturah, and is associated with the peoples of southern Arabia.

H7645G.name: Shebaniah
H7645G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7645G.brief: Priest who blew trumpets before the ark
H7645G.short: Shebaniah was one of the priests who blew trumpets before the ark of God when David brought it to Jerusalem.

H7645J.name: Shebaniah
H7645J.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7645J.brief: Priest who signed the covenant with Nehemiah
H7645J.short: Shebaniah was one of the priests who signed the covenant document during the time of Nehemiah, pledging to follow God's law.

H7645I.name: Shebaniah
H7645I.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7645I.brief: Priest during the time of Nehemiah
H7645I.short: Shebaniah (or Shecaniah) was a priest who served during the time of Nehemiah and is mentioned in the lists of priests and their descendants.

H7645H.name: Shebaniah
H7645H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7645H.brief: Levite who led the people in prayer
H7645H.short: Shebaniah, a Levite, was one of the leaders who guided the people in prayer and confession during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah.

H7669.name: Sheber
H7669.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H7669.brief: Son of Caleb and his concubine Maacah
H7669.short: Sheber was one of the sons born to Caleb and his concubine Maacah, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

H7644.name: Shebna
H7644.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7644.brief: Steward of the palace during Hezekiah's reign
H7644.short: Shebna was a high-ranking official in King Hezekiah's court, serving as the steward of the palace, but was later demoted and replaced by Eliakim.

H7619G.name: Shebuel
H7619G.desc: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H7619G.brief: Levite descendant of Gershom, in charge of treasuries
H7619G.short: Shebuel (or Shubael), a descendant of Gershom, was a Levite appointed by King David to be in charge of the treasuries of the house of God.

H7619H.name: Shebuel
H7619H.desc: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7619H.short: Shebuel (or Shubael) was a Levite musician appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals in the temple service.

H7609.name: Sheerah
H7609.desc: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H7609.brief: Ephraim's granddaughter who built three towns
H7609.short: Sheerah, granddaughter of Ephraim, who built Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah.

H7630.name: Shobai
H7630.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H7630.brief: Ancestor of a family of gatekeepers who returned from exile.
H7630.short: Shobai was the ancestor of a family of gatekeepers who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

H7629.name: Shobi
H7629.desc: Ammonite living at the time of United Monarchy
H7629.brief: Ammonite who provided supplies to David at Mahanaim.
H7629.short: Shobi was an Ammonite who brought supplies to David at Mahanaim when he was fleeing from his son Absalom.

H7643G.name: Sebam
H7643G.brief: Town in the territory of Reuben
H7643G.short: Sebam was one of the towns in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River (<ref="Num. 32:3">Num. 32:3</ref>).

H7614J.name: Sheba
H7614J.brief: Kingdom known for wealth, trade, and the Queen of Sheba
H7614J.short: Sheba, also referred to as the South, was a kingdom known for its wealth, trade, and the visit of its queen to King Solomon (<ref="1Ki. 10:1-13; 2Chr. 9:1-12; Ps. 72:10, 15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20; Ezek. 27:22-23; 38:13; Luke 11:31">1Ki. 10:1-13; 2Chr. 9:1-12; Ps. 72:10, 15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20; Ezek. 27:22-23; 38:13; Luke 11:31</ref>).

H7671.name: Shebarim
H7671.brief: Place near Ai where Israelites fled
H7671.short: Shebarim was a place near Ai where the Israelites fled after being defeated due to Achan's sin (<ref="Josh. 7:5">Josh. 7:5</ref>).

H7643H.name: Sibmah
H7643H.brief: Moabite town known for its vineyards
H7643H.short: Sibmah was a Moabite town known for its vineyards, allotted to the tribe of Reuben (<ref="Num. 32:38; Josh. 13:19">Num. 32:38; Josh. 13:19</ref>) and later mentioned in prophecies concerning Moab (<ref="Isa. 16:8-9; Jer. 48:32">Isa. 16:8-9; Jer. 48:32</ref>).

H7676.name: Sabbath
H7676.brief: The seventh day of the week, set apart for rest and worship
H7676.short: The Sabbath, meaning "rest," was the seventh day of the week, set apart by God as a holy day for rest and worship (<ref="Exodus 20:8-11; Leviticus 23:3">Exodus 20:8-11; Leviticus 23:3</ref>).

H7627.name: Shebat
H7627.brief: The eleventh month of the Jewish calendar
H7627.short: Shebat is the eleventh month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in <ref="Zechariah 1:7">Zechariah 1:7</ref> as the date of one of the prophet's visions.

H7641H.name: Shibboleth
H7641H.brief: A Hebrew word used to identify Ephraimites
H7641H.short: Shibboleth was a Hebrew word used by the Gileadites to identify Ephraimites, who could not pronounce it correctly, resulting in the death of 42,000 Ephraimites (<ref="Judges 12:6">Judges 12:6</ref>).

H7692G.name: Shiggaion
H7692G.brief: A musical term in the title of Psalm 7
H7692G.short: Shiggaion is a musical term that appears in the title of Psalm 7, possibly indicating a specific style or genre of music.

H7692H.name: Shigionoth
H7692H.brief: A musical term in the title of Habakkuk's prayer
H7692H.short: Shigionoth is a musical term that appears in the title of Habakkuk's prayer in <ref="Habakkuk 3:1">Habakkuk 3:1</ref>, possibly indicating a specific style or genre of music.

H7620G.name: Weeks
H7620G.brief: A Jewish agricultural festival celebrated 50 days after Passover
H7620G.short: The Feast of Weeks, also known as Pentecost, was a Jewish agricultural festival celebrated fifty days after Passover, commemorating the wheat harvest and the giving of the Law at Sinai.
